answer.rationale: The bottleneck is the write path under peak settlement load with a non-revertible release in place, so rollback is off the table. Circuit breakers (b4) apply to partner/dependency failures, which are not indicated; read-replica routing (b5) only relieves read load and won't help write latency; regional failover (b2) targets regional degradation, not capacity saturation. Adding write-path capacity matches the symptom and the closest precedent (b3: provisioning headroom absorbed a surge with queue depth staying flat), which I want verified before committing since it's my sole evidence for this action. I'll scale in a guarded increment first to confirm latency responds without destabilizing the heavy write traffic. Uncertainty remains: if the new release itself inflated per-write cost, capacity may only buy time, so I'll watch p99 closely and reassess at the next window.
